title: Template Variables and Filters
description: Insert dynamic data and transform it using built‑in filters.

slides.title: Variables: {{ ... }}
slides.content:
In your template, use double curly braces to output a variable that you passed from the view. **Example:** ```html

Hello, {{ name }}!

``` If the view sends `{'name': 'Alice'}`, the output becomes `

Hello, Alice!

`. Variables can be nested: `{{ user.profile.bio }}` (uses attribute lookup, dictionary lookup, list index).

slides.title: Using Filters |
slides.content:
Filters modify the value of a variable. They are applied with a pipe `|`.

```html
{{ name|lower }}          # lowercase
{{ price|floatformat:2 }} # 12.34
{{ date|date:"Y-m-d" }}   # 2025-03-22
{{ text|truncatechars:20 }}
```

quizData.question: What does `{{ user.name|upper }}` do?
quizData.explanation: The `upper` filter converts the string to uppercase.

slides.title: Passing Data from View
slides.content:
In your view, you pass a context dictionary to `render()`: ```python from django.shortcuts import render def profile(request): context = { 'username': 'johndoe', 'age': 30, 'posts': ['First post', 'Second post'] } return render(request, 'profile.html', context) ``` In the template: ```html

Username: {{ username }}

Age: {{ age }}

    {% for post in posts %}
  • {{ post }}
    • {% endfor %}
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `default` filter to avoid empty output

`{{ value|default:"nothing" }}` will show 'nothing' if `value` is missing or empty.
